providers.description: BookMyShow (Bigtree Entertainment Pvt. Ltd.) is India's premier online entertainment ticketing platform, serving as a centralized hub for discovering and booking movies, live music festivals, comedy, theatre, sports, activities, and Video-on-Demand (VOD) streaming. For enterprise partners and event organizers it also provides venue management software, box-office point-of-sale solutions, corporate vouchers, gift cards, and end-to-end event production capabilities. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel; enriched by the enrichment pipeline. No public developer API or portal was found, but BookMyShow publishes an agent-facing llms.txt describing its consumer inventory hubs and B2B services.

providers.name: Boletia
providers.description: Boletia (Boletia Mexico SA de CV) is a Mexican event ticketing, registration, and access-management platform headquartered in Monterrey, Nuevo Leon. Event organizers use Boletia to create and promote events, sell tickets online, manage attendee registration, assign numbered seating, publish billboards (cartelera) and venue pages, and control event-day access and check-in. The platform spans concerts, comedy and stand-up, sports, expos and congresses, festivals, theater, and workshops across Mexico, and provides the payment and infrastructure backend that powers ticket sales for its event organizers. Boletia is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Wanderu
providers.description: Wanderu is a ground-travel metasearch and booking platform - a Kayak-style aggregator that lets travelers search, compare, and book intercity bus and train tickets (plus flights and ferries) across hundreds of carriers in North America and Europe, including Amtrak, Greyhound, FlixBus, Megabus, Peter Pan, VIA Rail, and Deutsche Bahn. Its routing technology stitches together multi-operator bus-and-train itineraries, and bookings are completed in-platform with carriers paying a percentage of each fare. Wanderu operates a private booking/search API and publishes no public developer program, SDKs, or OpenAPI; its public open-source presence is internal engineering tooling on GitHub (the redis-backed "bamboo" queuing system). Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: ApniBus
providers.description: ApniBus is an India-based online bus ticket booking platform that lets travelers search routes, compare operators, select seats, and pay for tickets across government and private bus services. It positions itself as a leading Indian bus-booking marketplace and an official RSRTC (Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation) booking partner, aggregating over one lakh bus services across thousands of routes. The consumer experience spans a website and Android/iOS apps, with UPI, cards, net banking, and wallet payments, instant e-ticket / m-ticket confirmation, live bus tracking, and easy cancellation. ApniBus was surfaced as a portfolio company of Version One Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer or API program at this time.

providers.name: ScoreBig (TicketNetwork)
providers.description: ScoreBig is an online event-ticket resale marketplace owned by TicketNetwork, selling tickets to live sports, concert, and theater events with an emphasis on transparent, all-in pricing (no extra fees or hidden costs) and a money-back guarantee. Its parent, TicketNetwork, operates the Mercury Web Services API and Mercury Retail integration platform, an API-driven, real-time ticket-inventory feed offered to partners under contract. ScoreBig itself is a consumer storefront and does not publish a public developer API; Mercury is partner-gated behind a sales/onboarding contact form with a sandbox provided to approved integrators. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Shoobs
providers.description: Shoobs is a UK-based online events discovery and ticketing platform focused on urban culture — Afrobeats, R&B, hip-hop, dancehall, comedy, theatre, festivals, brunches and club nights across London and other British cities. Founded as a Y Combinator-backed startup, Shoobs helps fans find and book tickets to events that match their taste, and lets promoters list and sell tickets for urban and Black-British cultural events. The platform pairs an events listing and discovery site with an integrated editorial blog covering artists, concerts and nightlife. Shoobs is a consumer web product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Jump
providers.description: Jump is a unified fan experience and ticketing platform built exclusively for professional sports teams. It combines primary and resale ticketing, team-branded mobile apps and websites, marketing and messaging, loyalty, fan identity and wallet, point-of-sale and scanning, dynamic pricing, and a unified fan-data foundation into a single system that teams own and control. Jump also embeds agentic AI agents to automate pricing, inventory, and revenue operations. It serves teams across the NBA, MLB, WNBA, NWSL, USL, and NCAA and is backed by Battery Ventures, Forerunner Ventures, Index Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. Jump connects to the tools teams already use through integration APIs, but publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or self-serve API documentation.

providers.name: Season Share
providers.description: Season Share (SeasonShare) is a ticketing technology platform for sports and entertainment venues. Its subscription-pass, last-minute, student, and credit-based products — Pass, Flow, Flex, and LivePass — help teams and venues reach younger fans, capture first-party data, and build recurring ticket revenue. It reports $100M+ in ticket inventory delivered and 1.5M tickets purchased, and is used by 30+ franchises including the Sacramento Kings, New Jersey Devils, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Nashville Predators. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company; no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: SilverRail
providers.description: SilverRail Technologies is a rail technology company that powers global rail ecommerce and distribution. Its platform spans journey planning, ticketing, and onboard information, aiming to transform the rail experience for travelers while making rail retail easier and more profitable for operators, travel agencies, and distributors. SilverRail connects rail carriers and sellers so rail inventory can be searched, booked, and ticketed across markets. The company was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Accel and Canaan Partners. As of this enrichment pass SilverRail runs a corporate marketing site (Next.js) but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery documents; its API and distribution capabilities appear to be delivered through partner/enterprise integration rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Hudl
providers.description: Hudl is a Lincoln, Nebraska sports performance and analytics technology company founded in 2007. The company started as a video sharing and review platform for high school, college, and professional teams and has grown into a global provider of video capture hardware, performance analysis software, and sports data services. Hudl operates across basketball, baseball, football, ice hockey, rugby, soccer, softball, and volleyball, serving customers from youth clubs through professional leagues. The company's product portfolio spans the core Hudl video platform, Hudl Focus AI-powered capture cameras (Indoor, Outdoor, Flex, Point), Hudl Replay and Hudl Studio for live and tactical analysis, Hudl IQ for American football analytics, Volleymetrics, the Hudl TV livestreaming product, and Hudl Tickets digital ticketing. Through acquisitions Hudl has consolidated several leading performance analysis and football data brands under its umbrella, including Sportscode (performance analysis software), Wyscout (the largest soccer video and stats database), Statsbomb (advanced football analytics), Instat (video and scouting), WIMU and Titan (athlete tracking and wearables), and Signal and ADI. Hudl exposes commercial developer surfaces primarily through Hudl Wyscout (Wyscout Data API, documented as OpenAPI 3.0 at apidocs.wyscout.com, with Database, Stats, Events, and Physical Data packs) and Hudl Statsbomb (the Statsbomb Aggregated API for player-match, player-season, team-match, and team-season data, accessed via the Data Hub, plus the Raw X&Y Tracking Data API and a Wyscout/Statsbomb ID Mapping API). Core Hudl video and Hudl Focus do not publish a public developer API; B2B integrations are sales-mediated. Hudl maintains a public GitHub organization (github.com/hudl) with infrastructure, resilience, and media tooling open source projects (Mjolnir, Fargo, HudlFfmpeg, react-native components), but these are engineering libraries, not product SDKs. Hudl's revenue model is SaaS subscriptions for video, analytics, and data packages, plus camera hardware sales and data licensing.

providers.name: Let's Do This
providers.description: Let's Do This is an endurance-events marketplace where participants discover and register for mass-participation sport — marathons, road races, trail runs, triathlons, obstacle races and cycling events — across the United Kingdom and the United States. The platform covers event discovery, entry purchase and entry management, team entries, memberships, referral credits and discount codes, and it works with event organisers and charity partners who list and sell places through it. Backed by EQT Ventures. As of July 2026 Let's Do This publishes no public API program: there is no developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable specification, SDK or webhook surface. A live but undocumented GraphQL endpoint backs the consumer marketplace with introspection disabled.

providers.name: Grassroots Unwired
providers.description: Grassroots Unwired is a mobile-first platform for face-to-face (F2F) outreach, advocacy, and fundraising, purpose-built for political campaigns, nonprofits, labor unions, and community organizations. Its offline-capable mobile apps let field teams run GPS-enabled door-to-door canvassing, capture in-person and peer-to-peer donations, send SMS and digital content from the field, and manage event check-in, registration, and merchandise operations for 4EventDay. The platform keeps collecting data, donations, and check-ins even when Wi-Fi and cell coverage are spotty, then syncs in real time with major CRM, donor, and payment systems (EveryAction, NGP VAN, Blackbaud Luminate, NeonCRM, Stripe, and others).

providers.name: Project Admission
providers.description: Project Admission is a ticketing technology company serving the live event industry — professional sports teams, leagues, artists, theaters, and venues. It layers on top of existing ticketing systems such as SeatGeek, Ticketmaster, and AXS to expand opportunities around the ticket and capture more value before, during, and after an event. Its platform provides branded storefronts, multi-channel inventory management, bulk ticket distribution, split season-ticket ingestion, and fan-engagement tools including influencer and group-sales programs. Project Admission does not publicly expose a developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its verified public web and security surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ring Radar
providers.description: Ring Radar is horse show management software for the equestrian industry, operating at ringradar.com. The web-based platform helps horse show organizers, managers, and exhibitors run competitions end to end - handling show entries, class scheduling, ring coordination, results, and exhibitor information. Ring Radar is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile the company runs a consumer web application (login and signup) but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, or developer documentation surface that could be discovered.

providers.name: Filmgrail
providers.description: Filmgrail is an Oslo, Norway based software company offering an AI-powered digital platform for cinema operators. Its product suite bundles a cinema content management system (CMS), native iOS and Android mobile apps, branded cinema websites, and marketing and analytics tooling into a single managed offering, with a loyalty system, festival platform, push notifications, and a planning tool layered on top. Filmgrail markets these capabilities as a way to automate cinema operations and grow digital ticket sales and moviegoer engagement, and describes API-based integration between its platform and cinema point-of-sale systems, websites, and mobile apps. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from Oslo, Norway and Delaware, USA. Filmgrail does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs; this profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record.

providers.name: Eventtus
providers.description: Eventtus was a Cairo, Egypt-based event technology company that built a mobile event app and attendee-engagement platform for conferences, trade shows, and community events. Its product offered event apps with agendas, networking and matchmaking, live Q&A and polls, push notifications, social feeds, lead capture, badge printing, online registration, and organizer analytics. Founded by Mai Medhat and Nihal Fares, Eventtus raised venture funding from investors including 500 Startups (500 Global), Vodafone Ventures, and Endure Capital, and was acquired by the community-events platform Bevy in July 2021. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment found no live public API, developer portal, or first-party SDK — the eventtus.com domain no longer resolves and the engineering blog is offline — so the profile is retained as identity only.

providers.name: Sofar Sounds
providers.description: Sofar Sounds curates secret, intimate live-music gigs in living rooms, small venues, and unexpected spaces in hundreds of cities around the world. The company connects independent and emerging artists with attentive local audiences through a mobile-first ticketing and events platform, and works with hosts who lend their spaces for the shows. Sofar operates a consumer-facing website and apps rather than a public developer program; probing its surface confirmed no documented public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI. It runs a real GitHub organization (github.com/sofarsounds) of internal engineering repositories, and its production backend is served from api.sofarsounds.com (Heroku), but neither exposes a published, documented API for third-party developers.

providers.name: Blink Identity
providers.description: Blink Identity is an Austin, Texas company building a privacy-first facial-recognition identity platform for live entertainment venues, stadiums, and public spaces. Its "identify-in-motion" machine-vision system lets patrons enroll with a smartphone photo, then walk through touchless entry, pay-with-your-face concessions, and automatic loyalty recognition without stopping to scan a ticket. Facial images are converted into encrypted templates rather than stored as photos, and the company is a Techstars Music alumnus that has partnered with Live Nation / Ticketmaster on facial-recognition ticketing. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website; Blink Identity does not currently publish a developer-facing API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Customer Portals
providers.description: Customer Portals is the topic dedicated to the architecture, APIs, schemas, and reference designs behind self-service customer portals. A customer portal is a secure web or mobile experience where authenticated customers can manage their profile, view orders and invoices, pay bills, submit and track support tickets, download documents, manage notification preferences, and access account-specific resources. Modern customer portals are typically composed of multiple back-end APIs - authentication and identity, profile and preference management, billing and invoicing, support and ticketing, notifications, and document delivery - surfaced through a single front-end shell. This repository tracks the vendors, patterns, and standards that make customer portals reliable, accessible, and API-driven.

providers.name: Fanimal
providers.description: Fanimal was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Re-verified on 2026-07-20, the primary domain fanimal.com remains a parked, Cloudflare-fronted redirect — every path probed (root, /llms.txt, /.well-known/security.txt, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/api-catalog, and the api./developer./docs. subdomains) returns HTTP 301 to https://tickpick.com/?fanimal=y. The ?fanimal=y attribution marker on a redirect into a ticket-resale marketplace indicates the property is defunct or has been absorbed by TickPick. No package was found on npm, PyPI, RubyGems, or crates.io; the github.com/Fanimal organization exists but is empty (0 public repos, no profile metadata) and cannot be verified as the same company. No independent Fanimal API, developer portal, OpenAPI spec, MCP server, or reachable /.well-known/ surface exists to enrich; there is no spec-bearing developer surface to ground any artifact against. The registered domain is still administered (live TLS, HSTS, SES SPF, Google and Klaviyo site-verification TXT records), which is captured in the probed domain-security artifact.

providers.name: Flixster
providers.description: Flixster is an American movie-discovery and social entertainment brand founded in 2007 that let people rate and review movies, browse local showtimes, watch trailers, and share what they were watching. It grew into one of the largest movie communities on the web and mobile, and in 2011 was acquired by Warner Bros. together with Rotten Tomatoes; Fandango Media later acquired both Flixster and Rotten Tomatoes from Warner Bros. in 2016. The Flixster Video digital-locker service (built on UltraViolet) was shut down in 2019. The flixster.com property no longer operates as an independent consumer site — it now redirects to Fandango, and Flixster does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/brand record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: MoreTickets
providers.description: MoreTickets (摩天轮票务), operated by Shanghai Juqitech, is a next-generation internet performance ticketing marketplace founded in 2015. The platform lets consumers buy and sell tickets to concerts, stage plays, musicals, and sports events through a transparent, competitive pricing marketplace with standardized ticketing services. It operates primarily as a consumer-facing web and mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API or open platform. The company is backed by Qiming Venture Partners and has raised a reported $108M in funding.

providers.name: Parature
providers.description: Parature was a cloud-based customer service and self-service knowledge base company founded around 2000 (originally as Cyracle) and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. Its SaaS suite covered a customer self-service knowledge base, ticketing/case management, live chat, and social customer service, and it exposed a developer API for managing knowledge base articles, tickets, and related data. Microsoft acquired Parature for a reported $100 million in January 2014 and folded its capabilities into Microsoft Dynamics CRM / Dynamics 365 for Customer Service. Parature from Microsoft stopped selling to new customers on November 1, 2016 and the standalone service was fully retired (end of support) on May 15, 2018. This is a historical/defunct company profile: the parature.com domain no longer resolves and there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Partyphile
providers.description: Partyphile (formerly Guestlist.ph) is a Manila, Philippines nightlife and events startup that built a consumer mobile app for discovering clubs, bars, parties, and events, getting on club guest lists to waive cover charges and skip lines, and booking VIP tables. Founded by Ron Baetiong out of a University of Santo Tomas thesis, it raised seed funding from 500 Startups (500 Global) and Kickstart Ventures and planned Southeast Asia expansion. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company presents no public developer or API surface — its primary domain partyphile.com no longer resolves and partyphile.ph is unreachable — so no API artifacts exist to harvest; this remains a company identity profile.

providers.name: Scoopola
providers.description: Scoopola was an early-stage consumer startup backed by 500 Startups (Batch 2, June 2011), pitched as "the HotelTonight for live music and theater" — a mobile app for discovering and buying last-minute, discounted tickets to local live-music and theater events. The company appears defunct; its associated web domains (getwillcall.com and scoopola.com) no longer resolve, and there is no surviving developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This record is retained as a historical portfolio-lead stub; the enrichment pipeline found no live API to catalog.

providers.name: Ticketfly
providers.description: Ticketfly was a San Francisco-based event-ticketing platform for independent music venues, promoters, and festivals, founded in 2008. It was acquired by Eventbrite in 2017 and, following a June 2018 data breach, was shut down in November 2018 with its music-oriented features folded into Eventbrite Music. The company is defunct: as of 2026 every Ticketfly host (www.ticketfly.com, developer.ticketfly.com) returns HTTP 301 redirects to eventbrite.com. No independent Ticketfly API, developer portal, documentation, or specification survives. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: yplanapp
providers.description: YPlan (operated by Leanworks Limited) was a mobile-first event discovery and last-minute booking app founded in London in 2012 by Rytis Vitkauskas and Viktoras Jucikas. It offered a curated feed of things to do and same-day ticket booking across cities including London, Bristol, Dublin and New York, working with thousands of event partners. The company was acquired by Time Out Group plc in October 2016 and the consumer app was discontinued in 2017. The yplanapp.com domain now 301-redirects to checkout.timeout.com. No public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface exists; enrichment probing found no API artifacts, so this remains an identity-only record for a defunct company.

providers.name: Sajilni
providers.description: Sajilni is a Middle East / MENA event ticketing and event-management platform built for organizers who care about data and branding. Organizers use it to create events, design branded registration pages, sell and scan tickets, manage seating and booths, run promo/discount codes, collect payments, and analyze attendee data. The consumer-facing site is sajilni.com with an organizer/business portal at business.sajilni.com; the platform is a Java/Spring web application with an internal authentication service at auth.sajilni.com. As of this enrichment pass Sajilni publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or webhook surface, so this profile captures the company identity, commercial pages, and a live domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Dreamscape Immersive
providers.description: Dreamscape Immersive is an entertainment and technology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Culver City, California, that produces story-based, full-roam virtual reality experiences in which up to six people share a physical stage and see fully rendered avatars of one another inside a virtual 3D environment. It operates location-based VR venues in the United States, licenses its platform to international operators, and is a partner in the Dreamscape Learn education joint venture. Its public surface is a consumer ticketing and booking website; as of August 2026 the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and the single backend its website calls is a private, key-gated AWS API Gateway host that returns 403 to anonymous requests.

providers.name: Qubit Smart Tickets
providers.description: Qubit Smart Tickets (Boletos Qubit) is a Colombian event-ticketing platform operating at boletosqubit.co, a Spanish-language consumer web application for buying and validating tickets to concerts, sports, and live events, with local payment methods including Nequi. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no publicly documented API, developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger specification, SDKs, changelog, or /.well-known discovery endpoints; the only server-side surface reachable is an internal PHP backend not intended for public integration, so no API artifacts were generated.
